EE5203 Lab 7 Guide

PWM and input capture: dim LD2, then measure the signal back - Basri Erdogan

Mission: Dim LD2 with a TIM2 PWM channel and step its brightness with button B1, with no HAL_Delay() anywhere. Then connect PA5 to PB6 with one jumper, measure the same signal with TIM4 input capture, and show that the measured period and duty match the values you set.

Prepare before class

Learning objectives

By checkoff time, you can:

  1. hand PA5 to TIM2 and generate PWM from the real 16 MHz clock;
  2. change the duty from code and from the SFR view;
  3. capture rising and falling edges on one pin with two TIM4 channels;
  4. turn capture timestamps into period, frequency and duty, wrap-safe.

Hardware and files

Item Value
Board Nucleo-F401RE: LD2 is on PA5, which is also TIM2_CH1
Clock HSI, PLL off (CubeMX step 2): timer clock = 16 MHz
Generator TIM2: 1 ms tick and PWM on channel 1, PSC 15, ARR 999
Button B1 on PC13 (GPIO_EXTI13, as in Lab 5)
Analyzer TIM4 CH1 + CH2 on PB6, PSC 15 (1 µs per count), ARR 65535
Wiring from Checkpoint C on: one jumper, D13 → D10 (figure below)
Tools STM32CubeMX (new project) + VS Code
Project name EE5203_L07_<studentnumber>
File you edit main.c, only inside the USER CODE regions

Configure in CubeMX

Start of the session: if C:\Work\<studentnumber> does not contain your Lab 6 project, copy all your project folders from H:\EE_Labs into it first.

  1. STM32CubeMX: Board Selector → NUCLEO-F401RE → accept the default initialization.
  2. Clock Configuration tab: System Clock Mux = HSI; AHB, APB1 and APB2 prescalers = /1. Every box on the right reads 16, as in Lab 6.
  3. PA5: click the pin and choose TIM2_CH1. It replaces the GPIO_Output (LD2) setting. Do this before step 4, or CubeMX may put channel 1 on PA0.
  4. Timers → TIM2: Clock Source = Internal Clock; Channel1 = PWM Generation CH1. Parameter Settings: Prescaler 15, Counter Period 999; PWM Generation Channel 1: Mode PWM mode 1, Pulse 0.
  5. Timers → TIM4: Clock Source = Internal Clock; Channel1 = Input Capture direct mode; Channel2 = Input Capture indirect mode. Prescaler 15, Counter Period 65535. Input Capture Channel 1: Polarity Rising Edge. Input Capture Channel 2: Polarity Falling Edge. Check that PB6 is now green as TIM4_CH1.
  6. System Core → NVIC: enable TIM2 global interrupt, TIM4 global interrupt and EXTI line[15:10] interrupts (B1 on PC13 stays GPIO_EXTI13).
  7. Project Manager: name EE5203_L07_<studentnumber>, location C:\Work\<studentnumber>, Toolchain/IDE = CMake → Generate Code.
  8. Copy C:\Users\Public\EE5203_template\.vscode into the project folder, as in every lab. (Own laptop: use Set Up STM32Cube project(s), as in Lab 5.)
  9. Verify, do not add: in main.c, MX_TIM2_Init() with TIM_OCMODE_PWM1 and MX_TIM4_Init() with TIM_ICSELECTION_DIRECTTI and ..._INDIRECTTI; in stm32f4xx_hal_msp.c, GPIO_AF1_TIM2 (PA5) and GPIO_AF2_TIM4 (PB6); in stm32f4xx_it.c, TIM2_IRQHandler(), TIM4_IRQHandler() and EXTI15_10_IRQHandler().

Step 3: click pin PA5 and choose TIM2_CH1. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Step 4: TIM2 with PWM on channel 1. Check the boxed rows. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Step 5: TIM4 with two capture channels on PB6. For Channel2 pick Input Capture indirect mode, not an entry marked DEPRECATED. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Checkpoint A - LD2 dimmed by PWM

TIM2 does two jobs from the same PSC and ARR: its update event is the 1 ms tick of Lab 6, and its channel 1 makes a 1 kHz PWM on PA5. Three additions:

  1. In USER CODE BEGIN PV, the millisecond counter, as in Lab 6:

    volatile uint32_t g_ms = 0;

  2. In USER CODE BEGIN 4, the tick callback:

    void HAL_TIM_PeriodElapsedCallback(TIM_HandleTypeDef *htim)
{
    g_ms++;                               /* TIM2 update: every 1 ms */
}

    Every callback in this lab has exactly one source, so none of them checks which timer or pin called it. A second timer or button would need that check.

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 2, start both jobs and set the duty:

    HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT(&htim2);                      /* 1 ms tick: g_ms   */
HAL_TIM_PWM_Start(&htim2, TIM_CHANNEL_1);           /* PWM on PA5 (LD2)  */
TIM2->CCR1 = 120;                                   /* 12 % duty         */

  4. Build (Ctrl+Shift+B), start the debugger (F5), Continue.

Evidence for Checkpoint A: LD2 glows, dimmer than full on. Pause; in the SFR view TIM2->PSC = 15, TIM2->ARR = 999, TIM2->CCR1 = 120. Write 50 into TIM2->CCR1 and Continue: LD2 is almost dark. Then write 1000: full on (CCR = ARR + 1). No code changed. GPIOA->MODER bits 11:10 read 10: PA5 belongs to the timer now. g_ms grows between pauses.

Checkpoint B - Brightness levels with B1

Each press of B1 moves LD2 to the next brightness level in a table. The button interrupt is the Lab 5 one; the 50 ms guard uses g_ms. Three additions:

  1. In USER CODE BEGIN PV, below g_ms, the press flag and the level table:

    volatile uint8_t  button_event  = 0;
volatile uint32_t last_press_ms = 0;
const uint16_t level[5] = { 0, 30, 120, 350, 1000 };  /* fixed CCR1 values, never written */

  2. In USER CODE BEGIN 4, next to the tick callback, the button callback:

    void HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback(uint16_t GPIO_Pin)
{
    if ((g_ms - last_press_ms) >= 50U) {  /* B1: one press per 50 ms */
        last_press_ms = g_ms;
        button_event = 1;
    }
}

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 2, below the three start lines, the level index; in USER CODE BEGIN 3, the step:

    /* USER CODE BEGIN 2 */
uint32_t idx = 2;                     /* level[2] = 120, as in Checkpoint A */

/* USER CODE BEGIN 3 */
if (button_event) {
    button_event = 0;
    idx = (idx + 1) % 5;
    TIM2->CCR1 = level[idx];
}

TIM2 holds the brightness between presses; the code runs only after a press.

Evidence for Checkpoint B: each press moves LD2 one level, 120 → 350 → 1000 → 0 → 30 → 120, and TIM2->CCR1 in the SFR view shows the same values. No HAL_Delay() in main.c. Predict, then check: change the table to { 0, 250, 500, 750, 1000 }. Which press changes the brightness most? Write one sentence: why does the first table look more even? Then put the first table back. Screenshot B_levels.png: the level table and your USER CODE BEGIN 3 lines.

Checkpoint C - Captures arrive

Fit the jumper from D13 (PA5, the PWM output) to D10 (PB6, the capture input). Both pins are on the same right-hand header, three pins apart:

Three additions:

  1. In USER CODE BEGIN PV, the results and the last rising timestamp:

    volatile uint16_t period_us = 0, high_us = 0;
uint16_t last = 0;

  2. In USER CODE BEGIN 2, below the PWM lines, start both capture channels. Only channel 1 gets an interrupt; channel 2 just captures:

    HAL_TIM_IC_Start_IT(&htim4, TIM_CHANNEL_1);   /* rising,  direct:   interrupt    */
HAL_TIM_IC_Start(&htim4, TIM_CHANNEL_2);      /* falling, indirect: capture only */

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 4, next to the tick callback, the capture callback. It runs once per period, on each rising edge. At that moment CCR2 still holds the falling edge just before it, and last holds the rising edge before that:

    void HAL_TIM_IC_CaptureCallback(TIM_HandleTypeDef *htim)
{
    uint16_t now = TIM4->CCR1;                    /* this rising edge     */
    period_us = (uint16_t)(now - last);           /* rising to rising     */
    high_us   = (uint16_t)(TIM4->CCR2 - last);    /* rising to falling    */
    last = now;
}

    No if is needed: TIM4 channel 1 is the only capture interrupt in this project. The uint16_t casts keep both subtractions right when CNT wraps.

Evidence for Checkpoint C: a breakpoint on last = now; is hit. Remove it, Continue, pause twice: TIM4->CCR1 differs between the pauses, and no line of your code wrote it. The hardware timestamps every edge.

See the result: add period_us and high_us to the Watch view (+). Continue, then Pause with no breakpoint set: at level 120 (after a reset) they read 1000 and 120, a 1000 µs period at 12 % duty; one press of B1 gives high_us = 350. Never read them at a breakpoint: the timers keep running while the CPU is stopped. They keep the last measurement, so if they look frozen, check that TIM4->CCR1 still changes between two pauses (pull the jumper out and try it).

Checkpoint D - Measure period and duty

This is what the two capture channels see on PB6:

Fill the Predicted column first. Read the values after a Pause, as in Checkpoint C.

  1. Press B1 until LD2 is at the 350 level (or pause, write 350 into TIM2->CCR1 in the SFR view and Continue). Pause and read period_us and high_us.
  2. Write 1999 into TIM2->ARR in the SFR view, Continue, pause, read again.
  3. Pause, write 999 back into TIM2->ARR, then 0 into TIM2->CNT, Continue. (CNT may already be past 999; from there it would never meet the new ARR.) Press B1 through the levels; pause after each press and read high_us. What do period_us and high_us show at level 0 and at level 1000? Why?
Quantity Predicted Measured
period_us with ARR = 999
high_us with CCR1 = 350
duty (%) = high_us ÷ period_us × 100
period_us with ARR = 1999
duty (%) with ARR = 1999

Evidence for Checkpoint D: the measured values match your prediction within ±2 µs, and you can explain the step 2 numbers. Copy the filled table into USER CODE BEGIN Header in main.c as a comment. Screenshot D_measure.png: period_us and high_us in the Watch view, and TIM4->CCR1, TIM4->CCR2 in the SFR view.

Individual extension - Overcapture or a servo (optional, click)

Optional. Open this only after Checkpoint D is shown and time remains. Pick one.

  • Overcapture. The timers keep counting while the debugger has stopped the CPU. Pause for a few seconds, Continue, pause again: TIM4->SR shows CC1OF set. Explain exactly which timestamp was lost, and why the callback could not read it.
  • Servo (if your kit has one). TIM3 CH1 on PA6 (D12), PSC 15, ARR 19999: a 20 ms frame, 50 Hz. Wire the servo signal to D12, its power to 5V and GND. CCR is the pulse width in µs: command 500, 1500 and 2500 (0°, 90°, 180°). If the servo buzzes at 500 or 2500, it is at its stop: move CCR 50 at a time toward 1500 until it is quiet. That value is your end point. Why can the servo not share TIM2?

Acceptance checklist

Individual oral check

  • Why does CCR1 = 999 give 99.9 % and not 100 %?
  • TIM2 makes a 1 kHz PWM and a 1 ms tick at once. Why does that work?
  • Why does the level table not use equal steps such as 0, 250, 500, 750, 1000?
  • Who writes TIM4->CCR2, and at exactly which moment?
  • Why is channel 2 indirect? What would a direct channel 2 listen to?
  • Captures 64000, then 1500: what is period_us, and why is the cast needed?

Submit

Submit main.c as it is at the end of the session (with the prediction table in USER CODE BEGIN Header), B_levels.png and D_measure.png.

Marks (10): pre-lab quiz on CATS 1 · A dimmed LD2 with SFR evidence 2 · B brightness levels with B1 2 · C captures arrive 1 · D measurement matches the prediction 2 · oral check (one question) 2. The extension is optional and not graded.

If you are stuck

Walk the signal from left to right and fix the first silent stage: TIM2->CCR1 value → TIM2->CNT moving → PA5 in alternate function (MODER bits 11:10 = 10) → jumper on D13 and D10 → TIM4->CNT moving → TIM4->CCR1 changing → CC1IF in TIM4->SR → NVIC enabled → breakpoint in the capture callback → period_us. LD2 stays dark? PA5 is still GPIO_Output in the .ioc (step 3), or HAL_TIM_PWM_Start() is missing. LD2 full on all the time? CCR1 ≥ 1000, or the TIM2->CCR1 = 120; line is missing. g_ms grows about 5 times faster than real time? The Clock Configuration tab is still on the PLL at 84 MHz (step 2). B1 does nothing? EXTI line[15:10] is not enabled in NVIC (step 6). One press skips two levels? The 50 ms last_press_ms guard is missing. TIM4->CCR1 changes, but the callback never runs? TIM4 global interrupt is not enabled in NVIC. period_us stays 0? The jumper is loose, or HAL_TIM_IC_Start_IT() is missing. high_us is 0 or larger than period_us? Channel 2 is direct instead of indirect, or its polarity is not falling, or HAL_TIM_IC_Start(&htim4, TIM_CHANNEL_2) is missing. period_us is a different number at every breakpoint stop? The timers keep running while the CPU is stopped. Remove the breakpoint, Continue, then Pause and read them. LD2 dark and g_ms frozen after you wrote 999 into ARR? CNT was above 999 and is counting on to the end of its 32-bit range, about 71 minutes. Pause and write 0 into TIM2->CNT.
